enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION C: READING COMPREHENSION (10 MARKS)**

*Read the following passage and answer the questions below it. Use your own words as much as possible.*

**The man-eating crocodile**

Babati is a very peaceful village. The people who live there are very friendly to one another and they never quarrel amongst themselves. They help each other in times of need and live happily. All the other neighbouring villages admire them. A great river crosses Babati. It is here that the villagers catch their fish, crayfish, and crabs for food. They make sure that they never pollute the water. They also have a large forest which is a sustainable source for food production, medicines, charcoal and construction materials. They protect their forest by planting trees each time they cut down a tree so that the habitats of animals, birds and other creatures are not destroyed.

One day, Layu, a famous fisherman and hunter in the village went out for his normal activities and did not return. Everyone was worried. The villagers wondered whether the people of other villages had caught him and taken him away or whether he had drowned in the river. Some people said that maybe he had been eaten by a wild animal. After two weeks, Layu's canoe was found stained with blood and the villagers concluded that Layu had been killed by a dangerous animal in the river.

The chief summoned the entire village for a meeting where he instructed them to stay away from the river because it appears that there's a big and dangerous animal in the river. He equally instructed the strongest men in the village to keep guard. After two days, they saw nothing but the chief encouraged them to keep watching.

A week later, Pa Fru, his wife and three children had gone to bed when they heard a noise behind the house. Something was moving and everyone in the house was frightened. Then something crawled into the sitting room and into the bedroom. It was a crocodile! Pa Fru's wife and their two daughters hid themselves under the bed. The eldest son, Sama grabbed a pestle and tried to scare away the crocodile but the beast opened its jaws wide to swallow him. Sama jabbed the pestle at the crocodile and the monster snapped its jaws then opened it again. Sama swiftly thrust the pestle deep down its throat and stuck it there. The beast began lashing out. Sama ran out of the house shouting at the top of his voice. Soon the entire village was up. The hunters shot the crocodile. From that day, Sama became the village Hero, he was nicknamed "the crocodile man" and the chief made him one of the most respected sub-chiefs.

*(Adapted from ANUCAM Educational Books PLC. 2nd edition, 2012)*

questions.enonce_markdown: **1.** What are the two main things that make the people of Babati rich and proud? *(2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Une question de compréhension de texte se répond en deux temps indissociables : repérer d'abord dans le texte l'information exacte qui répond à la question (la citation), puis la reformuler avec ses propres mots dans une phrase complète et autonome, sans copier le texte mot pour mot ni se limiter à une réponse elliptique.

Le barème d'une compréhension de texte récompense la précision de l'information relevée autant que la qualité de la reformulation en anglais correct : une réponse juste sur le fond mais recopiée telle quelle perd des points, de même qu'une réponse reformulée mais fausse sur le fond.

### Corrigé détaillé
Le texte cite deux ressources naturelles au deuxième paragraphe : « A great river crosses Babati... They also have a large forest ». Le fleuve fournit poisson, écrevisses et crabes pour l'alimentation, la forêt fournit nourriture, médicaments, charbon de bois et matériaux de construction.

Réponse : les habitants de Babati sont riches et fiers grâce à leur grand fleuve, qui leur fournit du poisson et d'autres produits aquatiques, et à leur vaste forêt, source durable de nourriture, de médicaments, de charbon de bois et de matériaux de construction.

### Conseil
Une question à 2 points en compréhension de texte réclame presque toujours deux informations distinctes et complètes : vérifie que ta réponse contient bien deux éléments séparés, pas une seule idée développée deux fois.

questions.enonce_markdown: **2.** What means did the people of Babati use to protect their forest? *(1 mark)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Corrigé détaillé
Le texte le précise directement : « They protect their forest by planting trees each time they cut down a tree so that the habitats of animals, birds and other creatures are not destroyed. »

Réponse : ils replantent un arbre chaque fois qu'ils en abattent un, afin de ne pas détruire l'habitat des animaux, des oiseaux et des autres créatures de la forêt.

questions.enonce_markdown: **3.** With evidence from the text, write two things that the villagers thought must have happened to Layu. *(1 mark)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Corrigé détaillé
Le texte énumère trois hypothèses des villageois : « The villagers wondered whether the people of other villages had caught him and taken him away or whether he had drowned in the river. Some people said that maybe he had been eaten by a wild animal. » Deux d'entre elles suffisent à répondre.

Réponse : les villageois pensaient soit que des habitants d'un autre village l'avaient capturé et emmené, soit qu'il s'était noyé dans le fleuve (une troisième hypothèse, moins reprise, envisageait qu'il ait été dévoré par un animal sauvage).

questions.enonce_markdown: **4.** How did they know that he had been killed by a wild animal? *(1 mark)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Corrigé détaillé
Le texte précise : « After two weeks, Layu's canoe was found stained with blood and the villagers concluded that Layu had been killed by a dangerous animal in the river. »

Réponse : deux semaines après sa disparition, sa pirogue a été retrouvée tachée de sang, ce qui a conduit les villageois à conclure qu'il avait été tué par un animal dangereux.

questions.enonce_markdown: **5.** What instruction did the chief give the villagers? Was his suspicion confirmed? *(2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Corrigé détaillé
Le texte rapporte deux instructions du chef : « he instructed them to stay away from the river because it appears that there's a big and dangerous animal in the river. He equally instructed the strongest men in the village to keep guard. » Le dénouement de l'histoire (l'attaque du crocodile chez Pa Fru, abattu ensuite par les chasseurs) confirme que sa suspicion était fondée.

Réponse : le chef a ordonné aux villageois de rester à l'écart du fleuve, car un grand animal dangereux semblait s'y trouver, et a chargé les hommes les plus forts du village de monter la garde. Sa suspicion s'est bien confirmée : un crocodile a effectivement attaqué la famille de Pa Fru quelque temps plus tard, prouvant la réalité du danger qu'il avait pressenti.

questions.enonce_markdown: **6.** Why did the girls and their mother hide under the bed? *(1 mark)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Corrigé détaillé
Le texte le dit explicitement : un bruit a été entendu, quelque chose a rampé dans le salon puis dans la chambre, et c'était un crocodile ; « Pa Fru's wife and their two daughters hid themselves under the bed », tandis que tout le monde dans la maison était terrifié (« everyone in the house was frightened »).

Réponse : elles se sont cachées sous le lit parce qu'elles étaient terrifiées en voyant un crocodile pénétrer dans la maison, jusque dans la chambre.

questions.enonce_markdown: **7.** If you were Sama what would you have faced the crocodile? Why? *(2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Corrigé détaillé
Question d'opinion personnelle et ouverte : il n'existe pas une seule bonne réponse, mais toute réponse cohérente, correctement justifiée et grammaticalement correcte doit être acceptée. Le corrigé qui suit propose un modèle de réponse complète.

Réponse modèle : Personally, I would have faced the crocodile in the same determined way as Sama, because freezing in fear would only have given the animal more time to attack. I would have grabbed the nearest solid object, such as the pestle Sama used, and struck the crocodile's head or eyes rather than its mouth, since the eyes are its most vulnerable point and its jaws are far too dangerous to approach directly. I would also have shouted immediately to alert the rest of the household and the village, because facing a dangerous animal alone is extremely risky and outside help can make the difference between life and death.

### Conseil
Sur une question d'opinion, structure toujours ta réponse en deux temps : la prise de position claire (ce que tu aurais fait), puis au moins une justification développée introduite par *because* ou *since*. Une opinion sans justification perd des points même si elle est grammaticalement correcte.
